quarterly-review.name: Quarterly Review
quarterly-review.summary: Rhythm-of-business arc for a quarterly team or department update: objectives, wins, progress, financials, challenges, lessons, next-quarter goals, recognition, discussion, conclusion. The team-facing sibling of Weekly Progress; for a leadership business review with asks, use Quarterly Business Review.

beats.name: Objectives
beats.description: Restate what the team committed to at the start of the quarter, with the measure for each. The audience should know what 'on track' meant before they see any results.

beats.name: Success Stories
beats.description: Lead with two or three concrete wins: what happened, who made it happen, and what it changed for customers or the business. Specific and dated beats general and enthusiastic.

beats.name: Progress Overview
beats.description: Score each objective against its measure with a simple status (met, partly met, missed) and the one number that proves it. Let the audience scan the whole quarter in one slide.

beats.name: Financial Performance
beats.description: Show the quarter's key financial metrics against plan and against last quarter: revenue, spend, margin or whatever the team is accountable for. One headline number, then the variance that matters.

beats.name: Challenges
beats.description: Name what did not go to plan and why, without blame. Pair each challenge with what the team is doing about it or the help it needs.

beats.name: Lessons Learned
beats.description: Turn the quarter into insight: what the team now knows that it did not know ninety days ago, and how that changes how it works.

beats.name: Goals Next Quarter
beats.description: Set the next quarter's objectives with a measure and an owner each. Fewer and sharper than this quarter's list is usually right.

beats.name: Highlights & Recognition
beats.description: Recognize specific people and contributions by name. Written recognition in the deck travels further than a mention in the room.

beats.name: Discussion & Feedback
beats.description: Open the floor with two or three framed questions, so the discussion lands on the decisions and trade-offs the team actually needs input on.

beats.name: Conclusion
beats.description: Close with the quarter in one sentence and the one thing everyone should do or remember next. End on momentum, not on the agenda.

technical.name: Technical
technical.summary: Engineers, data scientists, and technical specialists requiring precision, methodology details, and system-level understanding.
technical.description: Engineers, data scientists, and technical specialists who expect precision, methodology, and system-level understanding. Show the methodology and cite data sources, prefer technical diagrams to metaphors, and do not shy away from dense information. Chart density can be high; 20-40 slides is normal.

persuade.name: Persuade
persuade.summary: Change belief or win support for a specific argument, idea, or recommendation.
persuade.description: Use when the audience may be skeptical or undecided. Build a crisp thesis, support it with evidence, address objections, and end with a clear action.
persuade.outcome: The audience accepts the argument or supports the recommendation.

formal.name: Formal
formal.summary: Polished, restrained voice for board, investor, and regulator audiences.
formal.description: Authoritative without being cold. Use third-person constructions, full sentences, and concrete numbers. Avoid hedges and humor that depend on shared in-jokes; rely on clarity and precision to land.
voiceCues: Use third person and the corporate 'we' sparingly.
Lead with the recommendation, then evidence.
Quote concrete numbers; avoid round-tripping ranges.
Prefer full sentences to bullet fragments on key claims.
samplePhrases: Q4 revenue grew 18% year over year, led by enterprise expansion.
We recommend approving the Series B raise at $30M.
Net retention was 124%; gross retention was 96%.

minimal.name: Minimal
minimal.description: A clean, minimalistic theme with a focus on simplicity and readability. Ideal for professional, straightforward presentations.

burnt-orange.name: Burnt Orange
burnt-orange.summary: Warm orange and red accents for energetic commercial decks.
burnt-orange.description: A warm, high-contrast palette built around burnt orange, red, navy, and gold. It feels active without losing structure.

cool-horizon.name: Cool Horizon
cool-horizon.summary: Cool blue-green palette tuned for professional business decks.
cool-horizon.description: A balanced cool-toned scheme with deep navy, business blues, and teal accents. It works well across strategy, finance, and technical narratives.

bookman.name: Bookman
bookman.description: Bookman is a serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Bookman Old Style for both headings and body text.

aptos.name: Aptos
aptos.description: Aptos is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Aptos Display for headings with Aptos for body text.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
